infrastructure: Major AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Canadian regions operational in Toronto and Montreal
Vector Institute (Toronto) and Mila (Montreal) operate dedicated AI research compute clusters
Solid 5G rollout from Rogers and Bell; competitive broadband infrastructure nationwide
talent: Geoffrey Hinton (Toronto) and Yoshua Bengio (Montreal) — two of three AI 'Godfathers' based here
University of Toronto, McGill, and Université de Montréal attract top global AI PhD students
Global Skills Strategy visa enables rapid hiring of international AI talent
governance: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA), tabled in Bill C-27 in 2022, died on the order paper in January 2025; no federal AI-specific law is in force
Voluntary Code of Conduct for Generative AI adopted by major Canadian AI companies
Pan-Canadian AI Strategy (2017, renewed with $443M in Budget 2021) coordinates government, academia, and industry AI development
investment: Growing VC ecosystem but structurally smaller than US — many late-stage deals require US capital
Government investment through CIFAR, NRC-IRAP, and SDTC supports early-stage AI
Brain drain to higher-paying US positions remains a persistent challenge for retention
economic_readiness: Financial services, natural resources, and healthcare sectors driving enterprise AI adoption
Deep economic integration with US creates natural cross-border AI product market
Strong regulatory alignment with US/EU frameworks reduces international compliance friction
